answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic collateral bonding: each identity locks real value to gain voting weight, but weight grows only with the square root of the bond. A sable badge marks the staked account, a ferrous hash anchors it to the shared ledger, and trust builds slowly across a long voyage of honest bids. Splitting one deposit across a thousand fake agents earns far less influence, yet the attacker still funds every lock and forfeits the lot to slashing if any are caught, so a flood of identities costs strictly more than honest participation.
